experiments.title: Does GPT-4.1 catch the errors?
experiments.description: Mini generates four tasks; GPT-4.1 reviews the statements and solutions.
experiments.finding: All four were approved, including an incorrect algebraic simplification.
experiments.chart_note: These bars overlap: an approved task can still be wrong. They are not a correct/incorrect partition.

experiments.title: The same mini model as reviewer
experiments.description: Separate mini calls generate, solve blindly and audit four new tasks.
experiments.finding: It caught a false bijection claim but missed a conflicting domain.
experiments.chart_note: These are model decisions, not an independent measure of mathematical correctness.

experiments.title: Two reviewers, the same ten tasks
experiments.description: Five valid and five flawed solutions, with known reference labels.
experiments.finding: GPT-4.1 made better decisions, but its explanation still contained an error.
experiments.chart_note: Both models saw the same cases. Ten matching decisions do not mean ten error-free explanations.

experiments.title: Generate → review → repair
experiments.description: One complete repair cycle on fifteen tasks, followed by a fresh review.
experiments.finding: Model approval increased; the local count of mathematically correct tasks did not.
experiments.chart_note: Model approval and local mathematical assessment are different measures. Compare each measure only with itself.

experiments.title: V5: controlled numbers and mathematics
experiments.description: The model chooses a family; code supplies numbers, formulas and answers.
experiments.finding: Ten supported families passed their dedicated checks.
experiments.chart_note: 10/10 applies to curated families. It is not the accuracy of unrestricted LLM generation.

experiments.title: V5: seventy variants, seven topics
experiments.description: Controlled templates extended to induction, sets and other topics.
experiments.finding: Seventy variants across forty families passed their checks.
experiments.chart_note: Each bar is a share of the seventy-task set. This measures topic distribution, not correctness.

experiments.title: SymPy meets actual LLM generation
experiments.description: Forty close analogues and fifteen requested condition changes, with formal records.
experiments.finding: Checking an encoded calculation does not guarantee that it matches the written task.
experiments.chart_title: What the SymPy adapter could check
experiments.chart_note: Formal-record coverage, not task accuracy. Partial and unsupported results are not approval.

experiments.title: RAG: tasks from theory without examples
experiments.description: Retrieve a family, let the model choose, then compile fifteen numeric analogues.
experiments.finding: The required family was not always the first search result.
experiments.chart_title: Retrieval and selection on fifteen goals
experiments.chart_note: Goals were manually labelled. The bank and theory share their origin; this is a small controlled test.

experiments.title: RAG: one hundred analogues from two PDFs
experiments.description: Selected topics from course notes and Book of Proof; fifty supported families.
experiments.finding: Ninety-eight variants were admitted initially; two more after a retrieval fix.
experiments.chart_note: The first two bars measure context admission, not mathematics. One hundred variants are not one hundred distinct families.
